text:
🚨 ALABAMA EXECUTION TONIGHT — 6 PM CT / 7 PM ET

An elderly couple gave a 19-year-old Navy serviceman a ride home. He repaid their kindness by beating them to death.

Michael Shannon Taylor, 54, is scheduled to be executed by lethal injection tonight, November 5.

On November 4, 1991, Taylor was AWOL from the Navy when he encountered Ivan Moore, 83, and his wife Lucille, 79, in Gadsden, Alabama.

The couple knew Taylor and welcomed him into their home. Ivan even offered him a glass of water and a doughnut.

But Taylor had brought a metal bar in a duffel bag, which he left outside.

After eating, he retrieved the bar and brutally attacked them both.

When they were discovered two days later, Ivan was dead.

Lucille was still alive.

She died from her injuries on November 10.

Taylor was later arrested in Birmingham with the couple’s Cadillac.

In 1993, he was convicted of capital murder, and a jury unanimously recommended death.

Taylor had selected nitrogen hypoxia as his execution method, but Alabama instead scheduled a three-drug lethal injection.

Alabama’s protocol uses midazolam, a sedative; rocuronium bromide, a paralytic that stops breathing; and potassium chloride, which causes cardiac arrest.

The use of midazolam remains controversial because critics argue it may not reliably prevent an inmate from experiencing pain during the procedure.

Taylor’s attorneys challenged the change in execution method, but the court rejected their challenge.

Supporters also sought clemency, citing his age at the time of the murders and his reported rehabilitation. 

Governor Kay Ivey declined to intervene.

A few trade deadline notes:

The Jaguars are expected to ramp up their push for an impact defensive lineman following tonight’s game vs. the Ravens. It would be a major surprise if they don’t acquire one.

The Giants’ main focus remains Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, and they have made at least one offer to Indy for him. They want a big-time RB.

The Colts have garnered a ton of interest in DT Grover Stewart. They aren’t in a rush to deal him, but teams have been aggressive.

Josh Downs is a name that the Chiefs and 49ers have at least inquired about. He is expected to be dealt by Tuesday.

The Jets have spoken with teams about Breece Hall and Will McDonald, but nothing feels imminent at the moment. Another loss vs. the Chiefs could change that.

The Eagles and Chargers aren’t expected to have fire sales, but players on expiring contracts could be moved for the right price (Riq Woolen, Moro Ojomo).

text:
Wesley Pipes went into porn straight out of prison. He’d served three years for trying to carjack someone with a loaded gun. It was the first car he ever got caught on, he says, and when prosecutors offered a plea deal he took it on the spot instead of risking 10 or 15 years at trial. Out on parole, he couldn’t find much work, and he needed money for studio time for his music. So he called Players, a Black magazine from the 90s, and told them he wanted to get into the industry. They sent him to World Modeling, and he shot his first scene that day. He insists it was never about the women. For him it was strictly a hustle.

He started before Viagra and Cialis existed. Asked whether there was ever a scene where he couldn’t perform, he answered that he once had sex on camera with a 76-year-old woman. He hates admitting it, but her name was Shirley Ann and it’s all on film. When the cameras roll, he’s ready to go.

Born Wesley Lawrence in Mississippi in 1969, he took his stage name from Wesley Snipes and got into porn in 1998. The Internet Adult Film Database lists him in more than a thousand films. He went into the Urban X Hall of Fame in 2009 and the AVN Hall of Fame in 2015, and that same year a director announced Pipes had inoperable cancer.

He went from an armed carjacking to more than a thousand films and a scene with a 76-year-old woman. Did porn save Wesley Pipes, or was it just a hustle that paid better?

Fantastique: The Dreams and Nightmares of French Cinema Blu-ray - Catherine Deneuve, Fernando Rey, Marcello Mastroianni, Charles Vanel, Sandra Milovanoff, Fernand Gravey, Micheline Presle, Héléna Bossis, Jean Chevrier, André Reybaz, Adalberto Maria Merli @FilmsRadiance
US: https://t.co/oWLoNsoTXT

BONUS CAPTURES:

OUR REVIEW:
https://t.co/a2NwPLLsWe
Radiance's Fantastique: The Dreams and Nightmares of French Cinema makes a persuasive case that the cinéma fantastique is not a marginal curiosity but one of French cinema's most persistent and quietly radical impulses. Across nearly seven decades, these six films share a suspicion that the ordinary world is thinner than it looks, with dreams, desires, masks, and storms slipping through its cracks. Charles Vanel (The Wages of Fear, Symphony for a Massacre, Illustrious Corpses,) anchors two of them, directing and starring in the late-silent rediscovery Dans la nuit, whose masked quarry worker becomes a stranger in his own home, and returning seventeen years later in Edmond T. Gréville's wind-lashed Le diable souffle, again as a man whose love is threatened by an intruder. That film belongs as much to cinematographer Henri Alekan (Beauty and the Beast, Wings of Desire, Roman Holiday, Topkapi,) whose storm-lashed nights and sunlit idylls are a constant pleasure. Marcel L'Herbier (The Late Mathias Pascal, L'Argent, L'Inhumaine, Mosjoukine,) brings airy whimsy to Occupation-era escapism in La nuit fantastique, with Bernard Blier (Quai des Orfèvres, Le Jour se lève, Hôtel du Nord, The Tall Blond Man with One Black Shoe,) among its supporting players, while Jean Kerchbron's The Golem turns the borrowed-identity dream into something metaphysical and genuinely strange. Catherine Deneuve (The Umbrellas of Cherbourg, Repulsion, The Young Girls of Rochefort, Belle de jour, Mississippi Mermaid, Tristana, Donkey Skin, A Cop, Le sauvage, Hustle, The Last Metro, Manon 70, 8 Women, Le choc, The Convent, Belle Toujours, The Hunger, Pola X, A Christmas Tale, Marcel Proust's Time Regained, Dancer in the Dark,) uses her cool, unreadable persona as a weapon in Juan Luis Buñuel's The Woman with Red Boots, opposite Fernando Rey (Viridiana, Tristana, The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie, That Obscure Object of Desire, The French Connection, Chimes at Midnight, Illustrious Corpses,) whose casting makes the film feel like a knowing continuation of the elder Buñuel's tradition. The set closes with Raúl Ruiz (The Hypothesis of the Stolen Painting, Mysteries of Lisbon, Time Regained,) and his witty puzzle box Three Lives and Only One Death, in which Marcello Mastroianni (The Beekeeper, 8½, Divorce Italian Style, The Skin, Casanova '70, La Notte, The Organizer, The Bandit, City of Women, The 10th Victim, L'Assassino, Adua and Her Friends, La Grande Bouffe, Ginger and Fred, Marriage Italian Style, A Special Day, La Dolce Vita, The Law, Le Notti bianche, What?, Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow, Intervista, Property Is No Longer a Theft, Beyond the Clouds, The Sunday Woman,) in one of his final roles, glides through several lives with twinkling charm alongside Marisa Paredes (All About My Mother, The Devil's Backbone, Deep Crimson, The Skin I Live In.) Few of these titles have had any meaningful exposure in English-speaking territories, which makes the collection an act of genuine excavation rather than a greatest-hits package. Radiance's six Blu-rays offer consistently excellent, film-like 1080P transfers from new restorations, with The Golem a revelation and even the century-old Dans la nuit looking remarkably clean, lossless audio throughout, and a wealth of thoughtful new supplements anchored by the near-hour documentary on the cinéma fantastique then and now. This is one of the most rewarding Blu-ray box sets of the year and gets our highest recommendation!

text:
AI Can Wait for a Permit. Debt Payments Can’t. | November 6, 2026
📍Data From https://t.co/rtKhA53pFF Daily Report

Investors spent years asking: “How much AI capacity can companies build?”
Now comes the less enjoyable question:

“What happens if they borrowed for capacity that cannot open on time?”

Thursday delivered a brutal stress test.

🔻 Nasdaq Composite: −5.52%
🔻 S&P 500: −4.36%
🔻 Dow: −3.44%
🔻 Nvidia: −9.26%

The Nasdaq 100 fell roughly 6.4%, erasing an estimated $2.5 trillion in market value.

But the important story extends beyond the size of the red candles.
1️⃣ A construction delay can become a financing problem.
Election results have increased uncertainty around data center permitting, electricity access and local restrictions, particularly in major development hubs such as Texas.
For a project financed on the assumption that revenue begins next year, a substantial delay changes the economics.

Interest expenses continue. Equipment may depreciate. Additional funding may become necessary before the first meaningful cash receipts arrive.

An order backlog can support a business case. It cannot automatically solve a mismatch between payment deadlines and cash collection.

2️⃣ Suppliers face a timing problem—even if AI demand survives.

The bearish scenario does not require everyone to stop using AI.

A slower rollout could push chip deliveries, infrastructure installation and revenue recognition into later periods. Investors may then lower near-term earnings forecasts and the valuation multiples attached to them.

Existing facilities, permitted developments and speculative projects also face different risks. Treating every announced gigawatt as equally certain was always an optimistic assumption.

3️⃣ Crowded positioning can turn repricing into a feedback loop.

When volatility rises, some systematic strategies reduce exposure. Options hedging and daily leveraged-fund rebalancing can add further selling pressure.

That can create a painful sequence:

Prices fall → risk limits tighten → exposure gets cut → prices fall further.

These mechanisms can amplify a decline. They do not prove that every seller is being liquidated—or that every fallen stock is mispriced.

4️⃣ Yesterday’s “safe” AI stocks offered only relative protection.

Cash-rich cloud platforms had helped support Wednesday’s rally. On Thursday, they fell too, although some avoided the supply chain’s worst losses.

That distinction matters: a stronger balance sheet can improve resilience without making a stock immune to lower growth expectations.

What would signal stabilization?

Watch whether project schedules hold, financing remains available, credit spreads stabilize and semiconductor shares stop making fresh relative lows.

A rebound driven by short covering can arrive quickly. A durable recovery needs confidence in cash flows.

The market is now charging investors for something the AI boom often treated as a footnote: time.

Wall Street suffered a massive selloff on Thursday, led by technology stocks, as the Democrats’ midterm victories fueled fears over the future of President Donald Trump’s ambitious AI investment drive.

The Democratic Party secured majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday’s elections, wresting control of Congress from Republicans. Candidates campaigning against new data center development also won gubernatorial races in Texas and Georgia, two states that have long offered tax incentives to attract technology investment.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged more than 5.5% during Thursday’s trading, erasing more than $2 trillion in estimated market value. The S&P 500 sank over 4%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which has less exposure to technology stocks, dropped more than 3%.

Semiconductor giants Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Micron and Broadcom were among the hardest hit as investors dumped shares in companies at the heart of the AI boom.

Trump Media & Technology Group and TAE Technologies Announce Effectiveness of Form S-4 Registration Statement for Proposed Merger

~ Files Definitive Proxy Statement/Prospectus as Combination Moves Toward Shareholder Vote~

SARASOTA, Fla. and HOUSTON, Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. (Nasdaq, NYSE Texas: DJT) ("TMTG" or "Trump Media"), operator of the social media platform Truth Social, the streaming platform Truth+, and the FinTech brand https://t.co/tevvTkgBvd, and TAE Technologies, Inc. ("TAE"), a fusion energy and power solutions company, announced today that TMTG's registration statement on Form S-4 (the "Registration Statement") related to the previously announced merger has been declared effective by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") on November 5, 2026. As a result, TMTG has filed a definitive proxy statement/prospectus and consent solicitation statement (the "Proxy Statement/Prospectus") with the SEC.

The Registration Statement registers the shares of TMTG common stock to be issued to TAE stockholders in connection with the all-stock business combination under the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated December 18, 2025. When the transaction closes, TMTG shareholders and TAE stockholders are each expected to own about 50% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis.

TMTG will hold a special meeting of stockholders on December 14, 2026 at 9:15 a.m. ET to vote on the proposals related to the merger. Stockholders of record at the close of business on November 2, 2026 are entitled to notice of and to vote at the special meeting and any adjournment or postponement thereof. TMTG expects to begin mailing the Proxy Statement/Prospectus to stockholders on or about November 6, 2026. TAE will seek approval from its stockholders by written consent. The transaction is expected to close by the end of the year, subject to the required TMTG shareholder and TAE stockholder approvals and satisfaction or waiver of the other applicable closing conditions.

“We’ve worked tirelessly with our colleagues at TAE to reach this milestone,” said Kevin McGurn, Interim Chief Executive Officer of Trump Media & Technology Group. “With the Registration Statement on Form S-4 now effective, we’re looking forward to bringing this merger to a shareholder vote and expect to close by the end of the year.”

Michl Binderbauer, Chief Executive Officer and Chief Technology Officer of TAE, said “For nearly three decades, our pursuit of fusion has produced advances in science and engineering that we are now bringing to market. This merger supports the next phase of that work, as we advance commercial fusion and apply the technologies developed along the way across power management and cancer therapy.”

TMTG stockholders are urged to read the Proxy Statement/Prospectus in full, including the risk factors. It is available free of charge on the SEC's website at https://t.co/4fpkHHeUO7 and on TMTG's investor relations website at https://t.co/QKreXkrTaU.

text:
After the 2024 Elections, we on the Right thought it funny that the Democrats blamed everything except their people and policies for their loss.  We said the Left needed to perform an "autopsy" to find the reasons for their shelacking.

After the undisputed Blue Tsunami in these Midterms, it would only be reasonable for us to stand back and be realistic about the GOP and it's supporters.

After the horrors of Covid, followed by the lawless tyranny and inflationary excesses of the Biden administration, we on the right falsely assumed that a decisive amount of swing voters saw things the way we did and would stay the course toward common sense.

Because we see how wacky, corrupt, and deviant the Left is, obviously any other decent human would agree with us, and vote "properly."

What I have seen among my own circle of friends is much more sobering, especially with the recognition that in Texas, many more registered Republicans voted this cycle.  And they voted Blue! (?)

This was a protest vote.  Against the Iran War.  Against the perception that those in control do not care about the day-to-day working class.  Against a scary future filled with data centers and AI.  All our candidates would gladly explain why Not to vote for their opponents.  But no one could clearly explain why one should vote For them.

We conservative activists, who follow the news from dawn to dusk,  know the stakes.  But our neighbors who take their news in occasional sips will see only what the networks and algorithms have packaged for them.  But this is not the time to blame mass media.  They have done the same for decades.

What this election told me is that many Americans still choose to believe in the old myths.  People find comfort in the innocence of yesterday.  They still believe "both sides" can be trusted to rule.

They want to believe we can have World Peace without personal sacrifice.  They want to believe Europe is still our old friend.  They want cheap, throw-away products made by 3rd world slave labor.  And most of all, they choose to believe that the Good Ole Democrat Party can be trusted to look out for the little guy.

They want to return to a world where Oswald acted alone.  Nixon really was a crook.  They want to believe DC is filled with well-intending bureaucrats who toil for a better future.  They want their cheap gardeners and construction workers.  And above all, they want cheap gas and groceries.

We know the Ukraine War has driven up global fuel prices.  But weren't we promised someone would end that in "24 hours?"

We know all the Covid stimulus drove inflation skyward.  Yet we were offered $5,000 each if we voted a certain way?

We know some states have exceedingly dirty voting rolls, yet our Senate refused to pass even a watered-down Voter ID law.

Trump has cut over 300,000 federal jobs, yet no one in Congress has mentioned how this could help with the budget.  And what that would mean for interest rates and affordability.  No one cited USAID or DOGE cuts while planning future spending.

In short, the Right has a long way to go in regaining trust.  In shaping narratives.  In making serious spending cuts. In building support for what has been a truly genius global foreign policy.

But future arguments must be made with the realization that the average voter needs to be massaged within their comfort zone.  Every departure from what they feel to be "normal" should be explained repeatedly and in the most basic of terms.

They do NOT believe as we do.  And this is OUR fault.  Digging out of this hole will be difficult.  But the future of America depends on meeting the voter where they are.  Not where we wish them to be.

text:
$DGXX CEO Michel Amar’s interview with Frank Curzio, key takeaways:

• ~$135M cash, zero debt and ~$155M invested into Alabama this year. Michel says construction is being self-funded.

• $200M straight debt financing targeted to close before Thanksgiving. He says the Goldman Sachs syndication secured a rate 2 percentage points below an earlier offer, saving ~$4M annually if fully drawn.

• Alabama Phase 1 expected complete in 7–8 weeks, with Phase 2 targeted for March 2027. All chillers for BOTH phases are installed and all equipment purchased. Around 250 people are working seven days a week on the 40MW IT-load facility.

• Initial Cerebras rent expected in December, with full rent from March 2027. Michel projects ~$6M MONTHLY EBITDA from March, equivalent to a ~$72M annual run rate.

• Michel says Cerebras wants all available DGXX power. However, DGXX is pursuing customer diversification, with 5–6 other contracts described as ready to sign, including some investment-grade customers.

• NVIDIA B200/B300 operations have been running since May with reported 100% uptime. Michel describes current income at roughly $1M monthly, while also citing ~$10M annually.

• Customers are reportedly accepting 30% upfront deposits for future GPU deployments. His illustrative example: a 3.6MW Vera Rubin pod generating ~$400M over five years could provide a $120M deposit to fund equipment.

• NeoCloudz launched its token factory in Berlin this week. Michel believes selling tokens can generate roughly twice the value of bare-metal GPU rental.

• Supermicro partnership supporting modular pod development for 2027. DGXX is also designing pods for Cerebras CS5/CS6 systems, with Vera Rubin equipment expected at the end of Q1.

• Within 36 months, Michel targets $500M+ annual revenue with ~25% EBITDA margins, implying ~$125M annual EBITDA at that revenue level.

• Michel estimates asset value above $400M versus the ~$225M market cap cited in the interview. He also highlighted New York preparations and potential West Virginia developments.

• No ATM use since June 13, according to Michel. He says he has never sold shares and is currently restricted from buying ahead of earnings.

• On equity compensation, he says awards are needed to compete for engineering talent. He described the intended increase as taking a 10% pool to 11%; the final proxy determines the actual authority.

text:
We can never control market movements or dictate when prices will rise or fall. However, we can control our response when the market crashes

1. If you know the market is approaching a bottom after a crash, the solution is simple: double down, buy the dip, and wait for the rebound. Once market conditions improve, your gains will be even greater

2. If you know the market is merely in the middle of a downtrend, you sell, then buy back in at a lower level at the very least, preventing further losses

Both responses to a market crash rest on a single premise: you have absolute clarity on where the market stands. But who can truly achieve that? Who possesses the ability to foresee the future? No one

Long-time followers will find this familiar. That’s right this is exact advice I shared on October 22nd. Word for word, I am sharing it again. Looking back now, do you see the value of these insights?

When a position is down by more than 30%, most people resort to a single tactic: doing absolutely nothing. Why? Because you assume that what falls deep enough must eventually rise, even if you don't know when. You assume that because a stock made you money before, it will do so again, even if you aren't sure whether institutional capital will select it during the next rally

Some even refuse to sell during a crash simply because they believe in the company and have developed an emotional attachment to it! Remember, we are here to make money. Mature traders must strip emotion out of their execution, right?

There is only one correct approach the one institutional firms rely on: hedging! You can short indices (SPY/QQQ), short individual stocks you hold, or seek cross-market opportunities just as we went long on crude oil and short on gold over the past few weeks (before adjusting our directional bias recently). Yet, most retail traders don't know how to do this. So, what should you do instead?

Opt for a simpler path: reduce your positions, follow market momentum, and execute short-term trades in assets you understand. Pick instruments with clear trends like crude oil, which exhibited a classic bullish setup this week, or gold, which shifted from a range-bound environment into a bearish trend. Trading the cleanest trends with flexible execution equals generating consistent cash flow in a bear market

The benefit of this approach is that once the market truly bottoms out, you'll have ample capital ready to deploy into high-quality companies. Take SPCX as an example: many bought in out of admiration for Elon. There's nothing wrong with liking the company, but many kept adding to their positions above $150. If the price drops to $100 which would be an exceptionally attractive valuation the tragedy is having no cash left to add

However, members in our group who have been following our short-term gold trades never have to worry about this. We are actively building up the capital needed to buy quality stocks at the bottom

Meanwhile, we have another blueprint: beyond accumulating prime stocks, we will allocate a significant portion of capital to TQQQ. If the Nasdaq falls another 5% to 10% (which is entirely possible), I will lead everyone into positioning in TQQQ. Historical data shows that whenever Nasdaq drawdowns exceed 20%, TQQQ typically rebounds by over 60%. This represents a high-conviction opportunity, so keep cash in reserve. This setup offers a far higher win rate than gambling on individual stock bounces

As long as you are in this group, I won't just warn you of downside risks (whether you listen is up to you), nor will I blindly preach doom and gloom. Instead, when genuine market opportunities emerge, I will lead you into high-probability bottom-fishing strategies. Combining individual equities + TQQQ + SPY + Gold, a 10% market rebound can easily translate into an 80% portfolio return or higher

Be fearful when others are greedy, and greedy when others are fearful. But right now is not the time for greed. When even the most steadfast bulls lose hope, that will be our signal to step in and buy the bottom

In the legend of Ys, the sea is both a literal force and a symbolic agent of judgment, memory, and the boundary between worlds, shaping the myth’s meaning across centuries.

🌊 The Sea as Divine Judgment

In most Christianized versions of the Ys legend, the sea functions as the instrument of divine punishment.

When Dahut’s sin or theft of the key unleashes chaos, the sea rises to destroy the city, acting as a physical manifestation of moral collapse.

The flood is not random: it is framed as God’s response to corruption, echoing biblical motifs like the Flood or the destruction of Sodom.

Gradlon’s escape—often aided by a saint—reinforces the idea that the sea punishes the wicked but spares the righteous.

This interpretation turns the sea into a moral force, not just a natural one.

🌊 The Sea as Memory and Echo

Breton folklore adds a haunting layer:

People say the bells of Ys still ring beneath the waves, especially during storms.

Some versions claim Dahut’s voice can be heard singing from the depths.

This transforms the sea into a repository of memory, preserving the city’s past even after its destruction.

It becomes a symbol of collective cultural remembrance, where the drowned city remains present, though unreachable.

🌊 The Sea as a Celtic Otherworld

Before Christian reinterpretation, the sea in Celtic mythology often marks the boundary between:

The mortal world

The Otherworld (Annwn, Tír na nÓg, or similar realms)

In this older framework:

A submerged city is not only a tragedy but a transition into another realm.

Ys becomes a Breton counterpart to other Celtic drowned‑land myths like Cantre’r Gwaelod.

The sea is a threshold, a liminal space where the living and supernatural intersect.

This interpretation emphasizes mystery, transformation, and cyclical natural forces rather than moral judgment.

🌊 The Sea as a Force of Nature

In coastal cultures like Brittany, the sea is ever-present:

Storms, tides, and coastal erosion shape daily life.

Submerged lands and shifting shorelines are part of environmental memory.

Thus, the Ys legend also reflects real-world anxieties about the sea’s power:

The flood becomes a metaphor for human vulnerability.

The city’s destruction echoes historical coastal disasters.

Here, the sea symbolizes nature’s supremacy over human ambition.

🌊 The Sea and Dahut: Seduction and Transformation

In Romantic-era retellings, Dahut’s fall into the sea is not only punishment but metamorphosis:

She becomes a mermaid (morgen), eternally tied to the waters that consumed her.

The sea becomes a symbol of seductive danger, mirroring Dahut’s own traits.

Her transformation suggests that the sea absorbs and reshapes human excess into mythic form.

🌊 Why the Sea Matters in the Ys Legend

Across versions, the sea is:

A judge (Christian moral tales)

A memory-keeper (Breton folklore)

A gateway (Celtic myth)

A natural force (environmental storytelling)

A transformer (Romantic symbolism)

Its shifting roles help the legend endure, allowing each era to reinterpret Ys through its own worldview.

The legend of Ys aligns closely with nautical Gothic themes, and its motifs echo real medieval events and saints tied to the sea and angels, whose stories help frame Ys within a broader Gothic spiritual landscape.

🌊 Nautical Gothic and Ys

Nautical Gothic emphasizes the ocean as a Gothic landscape—isolating, dangerous, and spiritually charged

The Gothic Library

This mirrors Ys, a city built below sea level and doomed by the sea’s mercurial power. Gothic sea narratives often feature:

Cursed wanderers (like the Ancient Mariner)
Ghost ships (Flying Dutchman, Demeter in Dracula)

Divine judgment through water
Ys fits this pattern: Gradlon’s city is swallowed by the sea after moral and supernatural transgression, a classic Gothic downfall.

⚓ Saints Connected to the Sea

Medieval saints often carried attributes that identified their stories

Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya
Several saints linked to the sea or maritime danger resonate strongly with Ys:

St. Christopher — patron of travelers, often depicted crossing dangerous waters; sometimes shown with a ship or oar in Western iconography
His role as a protector against watery peril parallels Gradlon’s escape from the drowning city.

St. Jude — symbol includes a ship, marking him as a saint of navigation and perilous journeys
St. Simon — associated with boats and oars, connecting him to seafaring danger
Our Lady of Navigators — depicted with angels holding her mantle and the Infant Jesus holding an anchor, directly tied to maritime protection
St. Columba — famously confronted a river monster in the Ness, saving a swimmer and converting witnesses
His miracle at water’s edge echoes divine intervention in Ys.

St. Brendan — his voyage through seas filled with monsters and supernatural phenomena
parallels the mythic Breton coastline where Ys supposedly stood.
These saints’ stories show how medieval Christians saw the sea as a place of danger, judgment, and divine presence, just like the setting of Ys.

👼 Saints Connected to Angels

Gothic art frequently depicted saints with angelic companions or attributes

Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya
These figures help frame Ys within a spiritual cosmology:

The Four Evangelists — represented by winged creatures (man, lion, bull, eagle)

forming an angelic symbolic system that appears in Gothic cathedral sculpture and stained glass
Mary, Mother of Jesus — often shown with angels, especially in Gothic altarpieces and rose windows
Her protective mantle imagery (Virgin of Mercy) parallels the protective role Gradlon’s daughter should have played.

Guardian angels — widely attested in saints’ testimonies as protectors and guides
Gradlon’s survival in Ys is sometimes attributed to angelic intervention in Breton oral tradition.
🏰 Gothic History and Real Events

Gothic art and architecture developed from the 12th–16th centuries
emphasizing:

Divine judgment (Last Judgment tympanums)

Saints’ lives depicted in stained glass and sculpture
Typological storytelling—Old Testament events prefiguring New
The drowning of Ys resembles real medieval disasters interpreted as divine warnings:

Floods destroying coastal towns

Storms sinking fleets

The collapse of Beauvais Cathedral in 1284, seen as a limit of human pride
These events reinforced the Gothic worldview: hubris invites catastrophe, a core theme of Ys.

🔗 How Saints and Gothic Motifs Inspire or Compare to Ys

Moral transgression → watery judgment

St. Columba’s monster story shows water as a site of divine power
Ys is destroyed after Dahut’s sin unleashes the sea.

Divine rescue of the righteous

St. Christopher carries Christ safely across a river
Gradlon escapes the flood, guided by divine warning.

Angelic symbolism

Gothic cathedrals used angels to signify divine oversight
Ys legends often include angelic intervention in later retellings.

Ghostly nautical Gothic

Phantom ships like the Flying Dutchman
mirror Ys’s spectral afterlife—some Breton tales say its bells ring beneath the waves.
When we pray for the dead, we do so not only for them, but also with them, drawn into a reciprocal relationship that the Holy Spirit brings to life in our hearts.

In the Bible, the sea symbolizes chaos, danger, divine power, judgment, and sometimes abundance, appearing as both a literal setting and a rich spiritual metaphor.

🌑 Chaos and the Unknown

In the ancient Near East, the sea represented uncontrollable forces and the mysterious depths of creation.

In Genesis 1, creation begins with God bringing order to the “waters,” showing divine mastery over chaos.

The sea often symbolizes the unknown or threatening, reflecting how ancient peoples viewed large bodies of water as unpredictable and perilous.

⚔️ Evil, Opposition, and Threat

The sea is sometimes depicted as a place where evil or opposing forces dwell.

In poetic texts, the sea is linked with mythical sea creatures like Leviathan, representing forces opposed to God’s order.

In Revelation, the beast rises “out of the sea,” symbolizing turmoil, rebellion, and worldly powers that oppose God.

🌬️ Divine Power and Deliverance

Many stories use the sea to highlight God’s sovereignty and saving power.

The Exodus: God parts the Red Sea, delivering Israel and defeating Pharaoh’s army.

Jonah: God controls the storm and the great fish, showing authority over the sea’s dangers.

Jesus calming the storm: In the New Testament, Jesus’ command over wind and waves demonstrates divine authority.

🌧️ Judgment

The sea is sometimes a tool of judgment.

The Flood narrative uses overwhelming waters to cleanse the earth.

Prophetic books describe nations being overwhelmed “like the sea,” symbolizing downfall and divine justice.

🐟 Provision and Abundance

Not all sea imagery is negative; the sea can also represent life and provision.

Fish and maritime trade appear as signs of economic abundance.

Jesus’ calling of fishermen and the miraculous catch of fish connect the sea with vocation, mission, and blessing.

🌅 Hope and Restoration

In later Biblical visions, the sea becomes a symbol of what will be overcome in the new creation.

Revelation’s phrase “there was no more sea” is often interpreted symbolically: the removal of chaos, fear, and evil in the restored world.

🧭 How These Themes Fit Together

Across Scripture, the sea is not one-dimensional. It is:

A real place of danger and livelihood.

A symbol of chaos, evil, and divine judgment.

A stage for God’s power and salvation.

A metaphor for spiritual struggle and ultimate restoration.

Democracy creates cycles of leadership change through free elections and accountability mechanisms, which can strengthen responsiveness but also introduce instability depending on how institutions function.

How democracy produces leadership turnover

Democracy places political power in the hands of the people through elections
In representative democracies, citizens elect officials who govern on their behalf, and these officials remain accountable through regular, free, and fair elections

https://t.co/EwFfeStNFv

This structure naturally creates situations where leaders are chosen, evaluated, and—if voters are dissatisfied—removed.

Two institutional models shape how this turnover works:

Parliamentary systems — The executive depends on legislative confidence and can be removed at any time through a vote of no confidence
This makes leadership highly responsive but also more vulnerable to rapid change.

Presidential systems — The president is elected independently for a fixed term and cannot be removed by the legislature except through impeachment
This provides stability but can also lock in unpopular leaders until the next election.
Across both systems, elections serve as the core mechanism for transferring authority peacefully, a defining feature of democracy as a method of public participation and contestation

Princeton University
Why democracies remove leaders

Democracy is built on popular sovereignty, meaning leaders govern only with the consent of the governed

Princeton University

When citizens feel their interests are not represented, they can vote leaders out. This reflects the principle that democracy is “government of the people, by the people, and for the people”
Other democratic features reinforce this turnover:

Political equality — Every citizen has an equal vote
Civil liberties — Freedom of expression and assembly allow citizens to criticize leaders and organize opposition
Rule of law and constitutional limits — Leaders can be removed for violating legal or constitutional boundaries
These mechanisms contrast sharply with authoritarian systems, where power is concentrated and dissent suppressed
Is this good or bad?

The answer depends on what values one prioritizes. Democracies offer clear advantages:

Accountability — Regular elections allow citizens to reward or punish leaders
Peaceful transitions — Power shifts without violence, unlike many non-democratic systems
Protection of rights — Democracies typically safeguard freedoms essential for participation
Better social outcomes — Democratic systems more consistently produce improved health, education, and economic results
However, democratic turnover also has drawbacks:

Instability — Parliamentary governments can fall frequently, especially in fragile coalitions
Gridlock — Presidential systems can stall when the executive and legislature oppose each other
Majoritarian risks — Majority rule can ignore minority interests without constitutional protections
Public dissatisfaction — Even in established democracies, citizens often feel performance falls short
______________________________________________________________________________________

The legend of Ys emerged in a period when democracy did not exist in Western Europe, which was instead dominated by tribal kingship, early medieval monarchies, and church authority, shaping the myth’s focus on rulers, saints, and moral order.

When the Ys Legend Took Shape

Most scholars place the origins of the Ys story between late antiquity and the early Middle Ages (roughly 5th–9th centuries).

Brittany at this time was populated by Celtic migrants from Britain, bringing heroic and mythic traditions.

Written versions appear much later (12th–15th centuries), but the core myth is older and reflects pre‑feudal Celtic society blended with early Christian influence.

What “Democracy” Meant in This Period

There was no functioning democracy in Western Europe during the era when Ys was imagined.

Instead, political life was shaped by:

1. Celtic Tribal Kingship

Power was held by warrior‑kings chosen from elite families.

Councils of nobles or druids could advise, but not in a democratic sense.

Authority was personal, sacred, and tied to moral legitimacy—a theme mirrored in King Gradlon’s symbolic key and his failure to restrain Dahut.

2. Early Medieval Monarchies

By the 6th–9th centuries, Brittany interacted with:

Frankish kingdoms (Merovingian, then Carolingian).

These were hierarchical, hereditary monarchies with no citizen participation.

Law and governance were enforced through oaths, fealty, and church oversight, not voting.

3. Christian Ecclesiastical Power

The Church was the most organized institution of the era.

Bishops and abbots held political influence.

Saints in the Ys legend (Gwénnolé, Corentin) reflect the Church’s rising authority over kings and communities.

Christian writers often used myths to teach moral lessons about obedience, virtue, and divine judgment, not civic participation.

Classical Democracy: A Distant Memory

The only “democracy” known in Europe at the time was:

Athenian democracy, long vanished.

Roman republican institutions, also gone by the 1st century BCE.

Medieval writers knew of these systems through Latin texts, but they were treated as historical curiosities, not models for governance.

How This Political Context Shaped the Ys Myth

The absence of democracy and the dominance of kingship and church authority deeply influenced the story’s themes:

King Gradlon represents the ideal of a morally upright ruler whose legitimacy is sacred, not elected.

Dahut’s rebellion symbolizes the danger of disorder in a society without participatory governance—where chaos comes from moral failure, not political conflict.

Saintly intervention reflects the belief that divine or ecclesiastical authority supersedes earthly power.

The destruction of Ys serves as a warning that a king who fails to uphold moral order loses divine protection.

Why Democracy Isn’t Part of the Ys World

The myth comes from a time when:

Society was hierarchical.

Power was personal and sacred.

Collective decision‑making was limited to elite councils.

Moral order, not civic participation, was the foundation of political legitimacy.

The Bible uses the sea as a symbol of God’s power, creation, chaos, judgment, and deliverance, appearing in stories, poetry, prophecy, and visions across Scripture.
🌅 Creation and God’s Sovereignty
The sea first appears in the creation narrative, where God shapes and bounds the waters, establishing order over chaos.
Genesis 1:10 — God names the gathered waters “Seas,” declaring them good
Psalm 95:5 — The sea belongs to God because He made it
Job 38:8–11 — God “shut up the sea with doors” and set its boundaries, showing His authority over nature
These passages emphasize God’s creative power and His ability to impose order on the untamed deep.
🌊 The Sea as Chaos, Danger, and Human Vulnerability
The sea often symbolizes danger, unpredictability, and human helplessness.
Psalm 93:4 — God is mightier than the roaring waves
Isaiah 57:20 — The wicked are compared to the tossing, restless sea
James 1:6 — Doubt is likened to a wave “driven and tossed by the wind”
These images portray the sea as a metaphor for inner turmoil, moral instability, and the forces beyond human control.
🌬️ God’s Power Over Storms and the Sea
Many verses highlight God’s ability to calm storms and command the waters.
Psalm 107:29 — God stills the storm to a whisper
Mark 4:39 — Jesus rebukes the wind and sea: “Peace, be still!”
Matthew 8:26 — Jesus calms the storm, revealing divine authority
These passages show that God brings peace in chaos, both literally and symbolically.
🛡️ Deliverance Through the Sea
The sea becomes a place of miraculous rescue and judgment.
Exodus 14:21–22 — God parts the Red Sea, delivering Israel and defeating Pharaoh’s army
Psalm 77:19 — God’s path is through the sea, even when His footprints are unseen
Jonah 1:15 — The sea calms when Jonah is thrown overboard, showing God’s control and discipline
These stories highlight God’s ability to make a way where none seems possible.
🐟 The Sea as Abundant Creation
The sea is also a place of life, beauty, and provision.
Psalm 104:25 — The sea teems with creatures “living things both large and small”
Genesis 1:21 — God creates great sea creatures and sees that it is good
Psalm 107:23–24 — Sailors witness God’s wonders in the deep
These verses celebrate the richness of God’s creation.
🔮 The Sea in Prophecy and Symbolism
Prophetic books use the sea to symbolize nations, chaos, and the end of suffering.
Revelation 21:1 — In the new creation, “there was no longer any sea,” symbolizing the removal of chaos and danger
Revelation 4:6 — A “sea of glass” before God’s throne represents perfect peace and purity
Isaiah 11:9 / Habakkuk 2:14 — God’s knowledge will fill the earth “as waters cover the sea”
These images show the sea as a cosmic symbol of both turmoil and ultimate peace.
📖 Key Chapters to Read
Several chapters provide deeper insight into the sea’s biblical meaning:
Genesis 1 — Creation of the seas
Exodus 14 — Parting of the Red Sea
Jonah 1–2 — God’s sovereignty over the sea and Jonah’s deliverance
Matthew 14 — Jesus walks on the sea
Revelation 21 — The sea in the new creation

Putin and Russia have repeatedly saved the Islamic Republic from collapse.

Much as they are doing again now, they have historically intervened when the regime and its allies were at their weakest.

The clearest example came in 2015, when Bashar al-Assad’s forces were losing Syria and the Islamic Republic’s intervention was failing to reverse the battlefield.

Assad controlled roughly one-fifth of the country. Rebel advances threatened the Alawite coastal stronghold, Russia’s Mediterranean naval presence and the Islamic Republic’s land corridor to Hezbollah.

The IRGC, Hezbollah and foreign Shia militias had kept Assad alive on the ground, but they lacked the airpower needed to stop his collapse.

Qasem Soleimani travelled to Russia in July 2015 despite a United Nations travel ban. He reportedly met Putin and senior Russian military officials, placed a map of Syria before them and explained how close the regime was to losing its most important Arab ally.

Soleimani offered the arrangement that would transform the war. Russia would provide overwhelming airpower while the Islamic Republic and its proxies supplied the ground forces.

Russia began its air campaign two months later.

The intervention rescued Assad, preserved Russia’s Mediterranean foothold and protected the Islamic Republic’s route to Hezbollah. It also demonstrated a recurring pattern. When the regime’s own military power proved insufficient, Russia supplied the capability needed to prevent a strategic defeat.

Eleven years later, the Islamic Republic is again under severe military, economic and diplomatic pressure, and another senior regime operative has been sent to Putin.

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and the Supreme Leader’s representative, met Putin on November 5 and delivered a message from Mojtaba Khamenei.

Rezaei is now setting the regime’s conditions on the Strait of Hormuz, nuclear negotiations and the post-war security order. His meeting with Putin reportedly addressed regional developments, assistance in ending the conflict and practical economic projects, including a proposed Russian gas pipeline intended to relieve the Islamic Republic’s shortages.

The timing matters.

On the same day, reporting based on leaked Russian defence-industry documents indicated that Russia had arranged to supply the Islamic Republic with 90 helicopter-mounted launchers for advanced guided missiles used extensively in Ukraine.

The relationship also includes negotiations or agreements involving Su-35 fighter aircraft, Yak-130 trainers, missiles and other military systems. The Islamic Republic previously supplied Russia with large numbers of Shahed drones for its war against Ukraine. Russia is now positioned to repay that assistance with weapons, diplomatic protection and economic support.

This is not an alliance built on loyalty. It is an exchange between two isolated systems that help each other survive pressure from the West.

Russia gains drones, energy opportunities, access to the Persian Gulf and a partner capable of disrupting American interests. The Islamic Republic gains military technology, diplomatic cover and an external power willing to prevent its complete strategic isolation.

The 2015 intervention shows why the current Putin-Rezaei meeting cannot be dismissed as ceremonial. Soleimani once went to Russia when Assad was approaching collapse and returned with the airpower that saved the Islamic Republic’s regional project.

Rezaei has now arrived while the Islamic Republic itself is under pressure.

Russia may not fight the regime’s war for it or provide every weapon it requests. Its support remains transactional and limited by Russian interests. But history shows that Putin does not need to rescue the Islamic Republic completely to change the outcome. He only needs to provide enough weapons, money, energy and diplomatic protection to keep it alive.

Russia saved the Islamic Republic’s most important regional ally in 2015. The question now is how far Putin will go to save the Islamic Republic itself.

After being humiliated in every election he entered, Mohsen Rezaei may now be the most powerful man in the Islamic Republic.

He is meeting Vladimir Putin, delivering messages from the Supreme Leader and setting the regime’s red lines on the Strait of Hormuz and negotiations with the United States.

His record reveals whom the Islamic Republic rewards:

▪️ Rejected by voters: Rezaei failed in every parliamentary and presidential election he entered. In 2009, he received less than 2 percent of the vote. In 2013, he finished fourth. Even during the heavily controlled 2021 election, invalid ballots reportedly exceeded his total.

▪️ Promoted after every defeat: Electoral rejection never weakened him. He continued accumulating power through unelected institutions answering to the supreme leadership and security establishment.

▪️ Former IRGC commander: Rezaei commanded the Revolutionary Guards from 1981 to 1997 and helped build the military-security apparatus that protects clerical rule.

▪️ Internationally wanted: Interpol issued a Red Notice seeking his arrest over allegations connected to the 1994 AMIA bombing in Argentina, which killed 85 people. Rezaei denies involvement.

▪️ Hostage-taking rhetoric: He publicly said it would be “great” if the United States invaded because the regime could capture thousands of American soldiers and demand one billion dollars for each hostage.

▪️ A son who defected and died mysteriously: His eldest son defected to the United States, criticized the regime and reportedly disclosed sensitive information. He was later found dead in a Dubai hotel under disputed circumstances. His death generated unproven speculation that the regime, possibly with his father’s knowledge, silenced him and that Rezaei placed political survival above his own son. No public evidence has established that allegation.

▪️ Control over war and diplomacy: Rezaei is now secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and the Supreme Leader’s representative on it. That places him near the centre of decisions concerning war, nuclear policy, negotiations and the Persian Gulf.

▪️ The regime’s voice to Putin: His November 5 Kremlin meeting showed that foreign powers are dealing directly with the Islamic Republic’s unelected security establishment, not merely its elected political façade.

▪️ Maximum confrontation: Rezaei has declared that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen and nuclear negotiations will not resume until the United States satisfies the regime’s demands. He called the latest American response insufficient and unconvincing.

This is about more than one unelected official. Rezaei represents a system that rewards loyalty, militancy and longevity while treating public rejection as irrelevant.

He never needed to win an election because elections were never where real authority resided. The Islamic Republic placed power in the hands of men who cannot be removed by voters, face no meaningful accountability and interpret diplomacy through hostage-taking, maritime coercion and permanent confrontation.

text:
Meet Martha Garside. She is seventy-four years of age, lives in a damp-coursed stone terrace just outside Holmfirth, and has never trusted a weather forecast in her born days.
Martha’s uniform is as fixed as the Pennine mist: thick, ribbed beige stockings that somehow manage to sag no matter how hard she pulls them, a stout navy skirt that has seen off three prime ministers, a pinny that smells faintly of boiled cabbage and carbolic soap, and a head full of curlers that she treats like crown jewels.
If you make the mistake of stepping on her meticulously scrubbed front flagstones with muddy boots, you won't get a polite cough. You will get the full force of her rolled-up Yorkshire Post, delivered with the sniper-like precision of a woman who spent forty years shouting at local lads for scrumping apples. She rules her patch of the valley with an iron ladle, viewing the local men—especially those daft enough to roll old tin baths down hills or build flying machines out of garden fencing—as permanent candidates for the local asylum.
Her conversation consists entirely of heavy sighs, sharp tucks of the chin, and observations on how nobody knows the value of a proper shilling anymore. She doesn't suffer fools, she doesn't do pleasantries, and if you offer her a cup of tea, she’ll check to see if you've wiped the spout first.

AI Assisted:

That same argument was made when the original legislation passed. Over time the system morphs, the exceptions expand, and we end up right back where we are now. There were competing arguments then that deserve to be brought forward again.

We don’t have to default to “we don’t have enough of X right now, so let’s import Y from country Z.” 

There are multiple ways to solve labor shortages using American workers: higher pay, better conditions, training, relocation incentives, and waiting for domestic supply to respond.

Immigration should return to a small, lottery-based system, plus marriage, with a limited, capped number of reciprocal work visas. Reciprocal seasonal work visas would also be reasonable.

The so-called “genius” visa is largely unnecessary. With modern communications and remote work, top talent doesn’t need to relocate here to contribute. 

The “talent” visa is worse in a different way: it undercuts the long-standing American idea that anyone can learn and improve. It accelerates the shift toward pure credential-chasing and treats ability as something that must be imported rather than developed. 

There’s also no guarantee their children will maintain that edge regression to the mean is common when starting from the top.

Why do we need these expansions now? A company can train a college graduate. A town can wait for someone to finish a trade certification. A hospital can raise pay and offer relocation assistance to get a nurse to Rock Springs, Wyoming, or anywhere else. Domestic adjustments take time, but they keep the system from permanently expanding.

text:
Annie Proulx’s Fine Just the Way It Is is a bracing collection of stories set in Wyoming, where the land is as unforgiving as the people trying to make a life on it. 

Proulx writes with a sharp eye and a wonderfully unsentimental voice. Her characters are stubborn, resourceful and often lonely; their troubles can be bleak, but the stories are lit by dry humour and vivid details that make their world feel unmistakably real. The landscape is never just a backdrop. It shapes what people can do, what they endure and what they dream of leaving behind.

The stories vary in mood and scope, so the collection is best taken one at a time, rather than rushed through. Some are grim, and Proulx rarely offers easy comfort or tidy endings. That honesty is part of the book’s power: life here carries on, often awkwardly, in the face of hardship and change.

A distinctive and memorable collection for readers who appreciate tough, beautifully observed stories and characters who stay with you.

text:
🚶 200 FACTS ABOUT KARL BUSHBY AND THE GOLIATH EXPEDITION, HIS 28-YEAR WALK AROUND THE WORLD

👤 THE MAN
1. ➡️ Karl Bushby was born on 30 March 1969 in Hull, England
2. ➡️ He grew up in the Sutton Park area of Hull
3. ➡️ He was badly bullied at school because of severe dyslexia
4. ➡️ His dyslexia was only diagnosed when he was 13
5. ➡️ He later described his school years as "hell"
6. ➡️ He found comfort in the outdoors, especially birdwatching near his home
7. ➡️ He joined the British Army at just 16
8. ➡️ He served 11 years with the 3rd Battalion of the Parachute Regiment
9. ➡️ He served in Northern Ireland during Operation Banner
10. ➡️ There he met his wife, Angela, a woman from Belfast
11. ➡️ They had a son, Adam, before divorcing in 1995
12. ➡️ His father, Keith Bushby, is a former SAS soldier
13. ➡️ He was 29 when the expedition began
14. ➡️ He was 57 when it ended
15. ➡️ The walk took up almost exactly half of his life

💡 THE IDEA
16. ➡️ The idea began with a birthday card from his father
17. ➡️ The card mentioned special forces soldiers arguing whether you could walk from London to New York via the Bering land bridge
18. ➡️ Karl sketched the route on a world map and decided to make it even longer
19. ➡️ He chose to start at the southern tip of South America instead
20. ➡️ Fellow soldiers told him it was impossible, which only made him more determined
21. ➡️ He named it the "Goliath Expedition"
22. ➡️ The Army first agreed to let him keep serving during the first 3 years and fund the trip with his signing bonus
23. ➡️ The Army cancelled that offer at the last minute, so he had to raise the money himself
24. ➡️ He left Hull on 5 October 1998 to travel to the start line
25. ➡️ He expected the walk to take about 12 years
26. ➡️ It ended up taking 28 years

📏 THE RULES
27. ➡️ Rule 1: no motorised transport of any kind to move the journey forward
28. ➡️ Rule 2: no going home until the unbroken line was complete
29. ➡️ He kept that rule even when family or friends died
30. ➡️ When he had to leave a country for visa reasons, he always returned to the exact spot where he stopped
31. ➡️ Every step of the route had to connect: "unbroken footsteps" from Chile to Hull
32. ➡️ Where there was water, he crossed it on foot over ice or by swimming
33. ➡️ He refused to use a train, car, plane or motorboat to move forward

🌎 SOUTH AMERICA (1998–2001)
34. ➡️ He set off from Punta Arenas, Chile, on 1 November 1998
35. ➡️ Punta Arenas is one of the southernmost cities in the world
36. ➡️ He started with a tent, a few hundred dollars and a cheap plastic camera
37. ➡️ He pushed a modified golf trolley full of gear that he named "The Beast"
38. ➡️ His route through South America crossed Chile, Argentina, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia
39. ➡️ In Colombia, locals warned he could be killed or kidnapped by FARC guerrillas
40. ➡️ FARC treated foreigners as possible agents of the US-backed Plan Colombia
41. ➡️ He crossed the Darién Gap, a roadless jungle between Colombia and Panama
42. ➡️ The Darién Gap is the only break in the Pan-American Highway
43. ➡️ Armed gangs in the Darién threatened his life
44. ➡️ He made it into Panama in February 2001
45. ➡️ He was then jailed for 18 days in Metetí, Panama, for entering without a visa
46. ➡️ In Medellín, Colombia, he met his next partner, Catalina Estrada, in 2000

🌮 CENTRAL AMERICA AND MEXICO (2001–2002)
47. ➡️ "The Beast" broke down in Nicaragua after about 3 years
48. ➡️ Its replacement, "Beast 2", stayed with him for the remaining 25 years
49. ➡️ He called the cart "my Wilson", after Tom Hanks's volleyball in "Cast Away"
50. ➡️ He walked north through Central America and the length of Mexico
51. ➡️ He crossed into the US at Nogales, Arizona, on 29 April 2002

🇺🇸 USA AND CANADA (2002–2005)
52. ➡️ When he reached Las Vegas in July 2002, his 90-day US visa had expired
53. ➡️ He couldn't renew it inside the US, so he flew to Bogotá to apply for a new one
54. ➡️ He then flew back and resumed walking from the exact same spot in Las Vegas in August
55. ➡️ On New Year's Day 2003, his cart was stolen while he was in a bar in Montana
56. ➡️ He spent a month replacing all the lost gear
57. ➡️ The stolen cart was then found in a quarry, just before he was ready to move on
58. ➡️ He crossed Canada heading north toward Alaska
59. ➡️ Bringing his partner Catalina along proved difficult, especially in Canada
60. ➡️ In late 2005 he tried to cross Alaska toward the Bering Strait
61. ➡️ He got as far as Unalakleet before spring thaw and his visa ended the attempt

🧊 THE BERING STRAIT (2006)
62. ➡️ By 2006 he had walked over 27,000 km (17,000 miles)
63. ➡️ From 17 to 31 March 2006 he crossed the frozen Bering Strait on foot
64. ➡️ He made the crossing with French adventurer Dimitri Kieffer
65. ➡️ The strait is about 93 km (58 miles) wide
66. ➡️ Moving ice forced them on a 14-day, roughly 240 km (150-mile) zigzag route
67. ➡️ It was described as the first recorded crossing of the Bering Strait on foot from Alaska to Russia
68. ➡️ They reached Russia near the Chukotka village of Uelen
69. ➡️ Russian border guards detained them for not entering at an official port of entry
70. ➡️ He spent 58 days in Russian detention
71. ➡️ He faced a ban that would have ended the expedition
72. ➡️ UK Deputy PM John Prescott, MP for Hull, raised the case with Chukotka governor Roman Abramovich
73. ➡️ On 5 May 2006 a Russian appeal court ruled in his favour and the walk continued
74. ➡️ A polar bear threatened him in Siberia
75. ➡️ He wrote the book "Giant Steps", first published in 2005
76. ➡️ Its 2007 edition covers events up to his Bering Strait crossing
77. ➡️ The book and the crossing inspired a board game called "Ice Flow"

🇷🇺 RUSSIA (2006–2017)
78. ➡️ Siberia's roadless tundra could only be crossed on frozen rivers and ice roads
79. ➡️ That meant he could walk only in late winter and early spring
80. ➡️ Russian visas also limited each stay to 90 days
81. ➡️ After the 2008 financial crisis he lost several of his sponsors
82. ➡️ From late 2008 to 2010 he lived in Mexico because it was cheaper
83. ➡️ New sponsors in 2010 got the expedition moving again
84. ➡️ He resumed walking across Russia in spring 2011
85. ➡️ On 25 April 2011 he reached Srednekolymsk after walking about 1,100 km that season
86. ➡️ In April 2012 Russia refused him a visa
87. ➡️ In March 2013 Russia banned him from entering for 5 years over a border violation
88. ➡️ In protest, he walked over 3,000 miles across the US from Los Angeles to Washington, DC
89. ➡️ His destination was the Russian Embassy
90. ➡️ The ban was later overturned
91. ➡️ His relationship with Catalina ended by 2011; he said "you can't have a relationship on the road"
92. ➡️ His son Adam briefly joined him on the protest walk across the US
93. ➡️ In all, crossing Russia took him around a decade
94. ➡️ He crossed from Russia into Mongolia in 2017

🏜️ CENTRAL ASIA (2017–2024)
95. ➡️ On 8 August 2017 he was in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia's capital
96. ➡️ He entered China in 2018 and crossed the Xinjiang region
97. ➡️ Local authorities restricted his progress there
98. ➡️ After the British Embassy stepped in, he continued under restrictions and a police escort
99. ➡️ He then walked west across Kazakhstan
100. ➡️ He entered Uzbekistan in June 2019
101. ➡️ He reached the border between Turkmenistan and Iran a few months later
102. ➡️ Visa problems and the COVID-19 pandemic then froze the journey
103. ➡️ Russia's invasion of Ukraine closed his planned route toward Europe
104. ➡️ Iran and Russia were both considered too dangerous to cross with a British passport

🏊 THE CASPIAN SEA SWIM (2024)
105. ➡️ To avoid Russia and Iran, he decided to swim across the Caspian Sea
106. ➡️ The Caspian is the largest inland body of water on Earth
107. ➡️ He set out from Kazakhstan in 2024
108. ➡️ He swam with Angela Maxwell and Azerbaijani swimmers Anastasia Boborykina and Abdurrahman Rustamov
109. ➡️ They swam two 3-hour sessions a day, morning and afternoon
110. ➡️ At night they rested and slept on support boats
111. ➡️ Each morning they returned to the exact coordinates where they had stopped
112. ➡️ The swim covered about 288 km (179 miles)
113. ➡️ It took 31 days and 132 hours of swimming
114. ➡️ He landed in Azerbaijan
115. ➡️ It was described as a world first

🌉 TURKEY AND EUROPE (2025–2026)
116. ➡️ From Azerbaijan he made his way to Turkey in 2025
117. ➡️ He crossed the Bosphorus in Istanbul into Europe
118. ➡️ In September 2025 he finished crossing Turkey and entered Bulgaria
119. ➡️ In October 2025 he reached Romania, about 2,213 km from the UK
120. ➡️ On 15 November 2025 he arrived in Budapest, Hungary
121. ➡️ In December 2025 he was reported in Slovakia
122. ➡️ Schengen rules allowed him only 90 days in any 180-day period
123. ➡️ He had to leave the Schengen Area and wait in Mexico in early 2026
124. ➡️ Two months later he returned to Hungary and kept walking
125. ➡️ By early June 2026 he had reached Belgium
126. ➡️ His visa ran out again, so he went back to Mexico to wait
127. ➡️ Eurotunnel refused to let him walk through the Channel Tunnel, citing safety
128. ➡️ In September 2026 France gave him special permission to swim the English Channel
129. ➡️ He resumed walking in Belgium, reaching Tournai on 18 September 2026
130. ➡️ He entered France on 20 September 2026

🌊 THE ENGLISH CHANNEL (2026)
131. ➡️ He swam about 21 miles (34 km) across the Channel
132. ➡️ He swam in stages over about 4 days, resting on support boats
133. ➡️ The start time and place were kept secret for safety
134. ➡️ He landed on Shakespeare Beach, south of Dover
135. ➡️ He reached British soil on 5 October 2026, exactly 28 years after leaving Hull
136. ➡️ His father Keith was waiting on the beach
137. ➡️ Filmmaker Werner Herzog was also there to greet him
138. ➡️ So was Commonwealth Games medallist Keith Jackson
139. ➡️ News of the swim only broke about 24 hours after he landed
140. ➡️ British immigration officers checked his passport on the beach
141. ➡️ He said arriving felt "almost like arriving in a foreign country"
142. ➡️ He kept looking the wrong way crossing roads after years of right-hand traffic

🏁 THE FINAL WALK HOME
143. ➡️ From Dover he walked roughly 250 miles north to Hull
144. ➡️ On 22 October 2026 he walked through Peterborough
145. ➡️ He reached Hull on 2 November 2026, 28 years and 1 day after setting off
146. ➡️ Hundreds of people cheered him in Hull's Queen Victoria Square
147. ➡️ He joked to the crowd: "Sorry to keep you waiting"
148. ➡️ An honour guard led the way on his final stretch
149. ➡️ Children lined the street to his mother's house
150. ➡️ He pushed "Beast 2" for the final steps
151. ➡️ His mother Angela greeted him under a banner reading "Welcome Home Son"
152. ➡️ They had not seen each other for about a decade
153. ➡️ He met his 12-year-old granddaughter for the first time
154. ➡️ Hull East MP Karl Turner read out a congratulatory message from the Prime Minister
155. ➡️ He said: "There was a big team. The biggest team: Earth."
156. ➡️ He said it took "two world records" to get home
157. ➡️ He became the first person known to walk an unbroken path from South America's tip to England

🔢 BY THE NUMBERS
158. ➡️ He walked about 50,000 km (31,000 miles)
159. ➡️ That is about 1.25 times the Earth's circumference
160. ➡️ It equals about 14 thru-hikes of the Appalachian Trail
161. ➡️ He took an estimated 75 million steps
162. ➡️ He was away for more than 10,000 days
163. ➡️ He crossed about 30 countries, according to the AP
164. ➡️ He crossed 4 continents: South America, North America, Asia and Europe
165. ➡️ He swam about 200 miles in total
166. ➡️ He used only 2 carts in 28 years
167. ➡️ He spent 76 days in jail: 18 in Panama and 58 in Russia
168. ➡️ The expedition was self-funded and relied on sponsors and strangers' help
169. ➡️ He spent 28 years without living in the UK

🗣️ IN HIS OWN WORDS
170. ➡️ "I'm an average guy… All I'm doing is putting one foot in front of the other"
171. ➡️ On finishing: "My purpose and reason for living is about to end"

text:
THE EVIDENCE™

Desperate for Headlines? Where Do They Dredge This Stuff Up Anyway?

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

The Seahawks have an injured quarterback, an offense struggling to find consistency, and plenty of questions about protection. Apparently, what they really need is another article suggesting they acquire somebody else to catch the football.

Heavy’s headline reads: “Seattle Seahawks Advised to Make Move After Sam Darnold Injury News.” That sounds consequential. Who is advising them? Someone inside the organization? A coach identifying an urgent personnel shortage? A source familiar with trade discussions?

According to the article, ESPN analyst Bill Barnwell suggested two possible additions: Philadelphia tight end Dallas Goedert and New York Jets receiver Tim Patrick. Heavy then built a story around those suggestions. The article eventually acknowledges that these are proposed fits rather than reported negotiations.

There is your answer to where they dredge this stuff up: another writer’s hypothetical shopping list.

An analyst can propose a trade. Another publication can examine it. But readers deserve a headline that reflects the substance: an outside analyst thinks Seattle could consider two players. Attaching Darnold’s injury gives the proposal urgency without establishing that Seattle’s front office sees either acquisition as the answer.

The injury news itself is real. Seattle announced that Darnold would miss the Arizona game with a quad injury, while Drew Lock prepared to start despite an elbow problem. The team also disclosed that Darnold played through a fractured rib against Chicago. Those developments warrant serious coverage of protection, preparation and how the offense will operate with its available quarterbacks. https://t.co/fGsHdxgPsb

Instead, the proposed remedy is another receiving weapon—or perhaps a receiver whose principal attraction in this discussion is his blocking.

Before we order more inventory, could somebody examine what is already on the shelves?

The Heavy article itself names Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton. Its discussion of another receiver even acknowledges the complications created by Seattle’s existing commitments and its desire to evaluate Horton. Those are substantial reasons to ask what another acquisition would accomplish, whose opportunities he would take, and whether the improvement would justify the price.

Seattle has pass catchers. The question is whether the offense can consistently put them in position to produce.

At tight end, Elijah Arroyo’s absence deserves an accurate accounting. He underwent shoulder surgery and is expected to miss the rest of the regular season. A deep-playoff return has been left as a possibility, without a confirmed date. His injury creates a legitimate depth concern. https://t.co/fGsHdxgPsb

But Seattle still has AJ Barner, Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup. Losing Arroyo does not mean the Seahawks have run out of tight ends. https://t.co/NBcaqyxzGA

Goedert might improve that group. That is a defensible football argument. It still requires more than reciting his receiving credentials. What would Philadelphia demand? How would Seattle use him? How much would he improve the offense compared with the players already available? And why should that acquisition take priority over other needs?

A recognizable name is the beginning of an argument, not its conclusion.

The same scrutiny applies to Patrick. Blocking from a receiver can contribute to a productive running game. But identifying a receiver who blocks does not establish that acquiring him would resolve Seattle’s difficulties sustaining drives. That requires an explanation of the actual breakdowns and how his role would address them.

There is a more immediate issue staring out from the injury report: keeping the quarterback upright.

According to Seattle’s account, Darnold fractured his rib on a blitz on the second offensive play against Chicago. That does not assign responsibility for every protection failure to the offensive line; protection also involves assignments, communication, backs, tight ends and quarterback decisions. It does establish a concrete reason to examine how Seattle handles pressure before declaring that another target is the next answer. https://t.co/fGsHdxgPsb

A receiver can win his route beautifully and still have no opportunity to catch the ball if the quarterback is already dealing with a defender in his lap. Another tight end might help with protection, receiving or both—but the analysis should demonstrate that fit rather than let the player’s reputation do the work.

That is the weakness in this kind of coverage. It is easy to identify an available player and describe how his strengths could help. Almost any talented player could help under favorable conditions. The useful question is whether the expected improvement warrants the cost, given the roster and the problems the team actually needs to solve.

To Heavy’s credit, the article identifies Barnwell as its source and discloses that no negotiations are being reported. There is no basis here to accuse the writer of fabricating a trade. Nor can we prove a personal motive from a headline.

We can judge the presentation, however. “Seahawks advised to make move” sounds more consequential than “analyst offers trade ideas.” Linking that advice to an injured quarterback encourages readers to expect a response to the injury, even though the proposed additions concern broader roster considerations.

Fans click expecting to learn what Seattle might actually be doing. They discover what somebody else thinks Seattle could do.

The verdict: Seattle has substantial receiving talent and three remaining tight ends. Arroyo’s injury creates a reason to evaluate depth, but it does not establish an urgent need to buy another pass catcher. A credible trade case must explain the role, the price and the priority—especially when protection and offensive execution remain central questions.

If there are negotiations, report them. If there is an analyst’s proposal, label it clearly and make the case.

The Seahawks need their offense to function. A headline needs only to attract attention. Readers should be able to tell which problem an article is solving.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

THE EVIDENCE™ | Kim Wojcinski — USA Best Selling Author

text:
We argued over presentations, competed over who could finish reports first, and occasionally exchanged sarcastic comments by the coffee machine. Somehow, those arguments became the part of my workday I looked forward to most.

Then one evening, we were the last two people in the office.

A heavy rainstorm had started, and Olivia was standing by the window, looking at the flooded parking lot.

"How are you getting home?" I asked.

"Apparently, by swimming," she replied.

I offered to drop her off. She hesitated before accepting.

During the drive, we talked about everything except work. I discovered she loved old romantic movies, hated waking up early, and secretly wanted to open a little bakery someday.

When we arrived at her apartment, she thanked me and stepped out. Before closing the door, she turned around.

"You're actually not as difficult as I thought."

I smiled. "Don't spread that around. I have a reputation to protect."

The next morning, she left a coffee on my desk with a small note.

For the man who argues too much but drives surprisingly well.

I kept that note in my drawer.
